frequency_question: What proportion of formal agency recognition revocation or termination proceedings initiated against a major institutional accreditor are fully completed, with all mandatory procedural steps exhausted and a final determination issued, within 92 calendar days?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative proceeding by the U.S. Department of Education (or equivalent federal regulatory body) aimed at terminating, revoking, or withdrawing institutional recognition of a national accrediting agency. Excludes voluntary relinquishments and minor compliance warnings that do not involve formal revocation proceedings.

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: Exhaustive review of federal recognition termination proceedings indicates that administrative due process requirements structurally prevent full completion within a 92-day window.
known_gaps: Limited number of total complete revocation cycles carried through to final judicial/administrative exhaustion within under 100 days.
skeleton: Regulatory review cycles (Notice of Intent, Advisory Committee Review, Public Comment Periods, Secretary Review) multiplied by mandatory statutory minimum calendar intervals required by the Administrative Procedure Act and Department of Education regulations.
multiplier: 4 distinct mandatory procedural phases * minimum required statutory/regulatory days per phase (averaging 60-90 days per phase, totaling minimum 240-360 days for complete due process)
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act and Department of Education institutional review regulations remain stable across multiple presidential administrations.
